title: Input
explain: The input() function pauses your program and waits for the user to type something on the keyboard. It returns what the user typed as a string (text). You can store this value in a variable to use it later in your program.
code:
name = input("What is your name? ")
age = input("How old are you? ")
print("Hello, " + name + "!")
print("You are " + age + " years old.")
exercise: Ask the user for their favorite color and their favorite animal, then print a sentence combining both: 'Your favorite color is [color] and your favorite animal is [animal].'
tip: Remember that input() always returns a string, even if the user types a number. If you need to do math, convert it to an integer first using int(input(...)).
